title: Personalized home feed architecture
description: Tests whether a model can find a complete, lasting, low-rent topology for personalized consumer discovery with high-follower skew, mutable visibility, and ranked derived state without being steered toward a preferred technology or feed strategy.
limitations: Ten million daily users is a population target rather than a throughput envelope, so the benchmark rewards topology continuity and explicit unknowns rather than invented capacity proof.
The task does not specify a learned-recommendation quality target, so a bounded heuristic ranking can satisfy the product contract.
outputContract: Recommend one concrete architecture in one or two paragraphs, followed by bullets naming canonical authorities, ownership keys, bounded request/background paths, and permanent components.

cases.task: Architect a personalized home feed for a consumer app that can grow from launch to 10 million daily users. People follow creators and page through a ranked mix of recent followed posts and recommendations, and some creators have millions of followers. New posts should be eligible within 30 seconds; after a deletion or privacy change is acknowledged, later feed requests must not reveal affected content to an unauthorized viewer.

scoring.judgeInstructions: Judge each anonymously labeled answer independently before comparing or ranking them. Score only the architecture's observable product completeness, authoritative versus derived state, horizontal continuity, bounded publish/read/rank work, component rent, visibility correctness, recovery, and cost. Do not reward any vendor, datastore, feed strategy, ML stack, protocol, service count, verbosity, or fashionable terminology. Compute-on-read, precomputation, and hybrid designs can each earn full credit when their bounds and tradeoffs satisfy the contract. Ten million daily users is not a throughput envelope: reward an explicit scale function and preserved unknowns, not invented capacity claims. A preferred technology earns no credit when its persistence, partitioning, recovery, or workload fit is unexplained. Use integer dimension ratings from 0 through 4, apply the lowest failed-gate cap after calculating the weighted score, and give concrete answer-specific reasons for every gate and rating.

gates.criterion: Publishing, following, personalized followed/recommended retrieval, bounded pagination, 30-second eligibility, and deletion/privacy behavior form one complete journey.

Content, follow/privacy facts, and any durable session state each have an unambiguous canonical authority and stable ownership rule; candidate lists, ranks, and copies are clearly derived or explicitly authoritative.

Launch and 10-million-daily-user operation use the same critical-path component graph, scaling by replicas or partitions; million-follower creators do not require unbounded synchronous work or a later topology replacement.
Confirmed writes are durable and retry-safe, and stale derived state cannot reveal deleted or unauthorized content on later requests; reconciliation or rebuild behavior is defined.

dimensions.title: Product fidelity
dimensions.criterion: How completely the design serves publishing, following, personalized ranking, bounded pagination, 30-second eligibility, and deletion/privacy behavior without inventing irrelevant product requirements.

anchors.0: Misses personalization, pagination, freshness, or visibility behavior.
anchors.2: Basic publish/read feed works, but session or mutation semantics are vague.
anchors.4: Defines the complete journey, ranking/freshness boundaries, pagination behavior, and sensible degradation.

dimensions.title: Authority and partitioning
dimensions.criterion: How clearly canonical content, follow/privacy state, derived candidates and ranks, stable ownership keys, and concurrent mutation boundaries are defined.

anchors.0: Conflicting sources of truth or ambiguous ownership.
anchors.2: Names source and feed state but leaves versioning, derivation, or mutation ownership unclear.
anchors.4: Defines one authority per fact, stable ownership keys, derived-state lineage, and concurrency boundaries.

dimensions.title: Horizontal scale continuity
dimensions.criterion: Whether publish, follow, candidate-generation, ranking, and page-read paths scale by bounded work plus replicas or partitions while preserving the same day-one topology, including for million-follower creators.

anchors.0: Contains an unpartitioned bottleneck, unbounded follower work, or later rewrite.
anchors.2: Broadly shardable but omits a major path or celebrity skew.
anchors.4: Publish, follow, candidate generation, ranking, and page reads all scale within the day-one topology.

dimensions.title: Bounded critical path
dimensions.criterion: Whether request work, fanout, candidate generation, hydration, ranking, pagination, and retry work are bounded per action and support interactive use.

anchors.0: A request scans the corpus or synchronously touches an unbounded follower set.
anchors.2: Common paths are plausible, but candidate, hydration, pagination, retry, or overload bounds are missing.
anchors.4: Every action has explicit bounds, including hot creators, ranking candidates, page assembly, and backpressure.

dimensions.title: Component rent
dimensions.criterion: Whether each datastore, queue, cache, ranking plane, derived copy, protocol, worker, and service is forced by a stated requirement and earns its failure and operating cost.

anchors.0: A service catalog with duplicate state and unforced ranking, queue, cache, or analytics planes.
anchors.2: Mostly coherent, with at least one permanent component whose removal is not shown to break the contract.
anchors.4: The smallest complete topology; every retained plane survives a collapse test and serves a sourced requirement.

dimensions.title: Failure and recovery
dimensions.criterion: How precisely the design handles duplicate publication, partial derivation, stale candidates, visibility changes, acknowledged mutations, reconstruction, and operational diagnosis.

anchors.0: Retries duplicate content, acknowledged mutations disappear, or stale copies leak restricted content.
anchors.2: Mentions retries or replication but leaves partial derivation, reconnect, or rebuild gaps.
anchors.4: Defines idempotency/versioning, fail-closed visibility enforcement, reconciliation, rebuild, and diagnosable degraded behavior.

dimensions.title: Cost and tradeoffs
dimensions.criterion: Whether cost follows bounded useful work and explicitly trades off read/write amplification, ranking compute, storage duplication, freshness, and high-follower skew.

anchors.0: Ignores read/write amplification, ranking cost, storage duplication, or unsupported scale claims.
anchors.2: Names broad tradeoffs without connecting them to demand or topology.
anchors.4: Relates cost to useful bounded work and states concrete triggers for changing freshness, ranking, or derivation strategy.
